title: Evening of 10-16: two freezes, the crash log, Dress Up 0.0.87 to 0.0.90
why: Matthew coming back after an hour away
summary: The laptop froze at 16:33 and 16:47, both during headless-Chromium runs; a new crash log lists 33 crashes since 08-18 and found the kernel sees no battery. Headless Chrome now runs pinned to 4 of 20 threads, with no crash in about an hour since. Dress Up 0.0.87 to 0.0.90 shipped still pictures on slow computers, opening doors, first collisions and N's pits; the day's 349 pictures were archived.

title: Late morning of 10-16: Dress Up 0.0.68 to 0.0.73, with Matthew and his controller
why: a shutdown to move the laptop
summary: Dress Up 0.0.68 to 0.0.73 shipped with Matthew and his controller: two jumps, the controller as a video game's actions, jumping in deep water, walking toward and away from us, and teach-me-your-controller with a SNES layout (^ticket(146)). The witch's places now run at 60 frames a second (^ticket(148)); Chrome's woods went from 13 to 56-59.5. ^ticket(145) is designed, not written; ^ticket(147) and ^ticket(149) were minted.

title: Morning of 10-16: after the 08:01 crash, Dress Up 0.0.62 to 0.0.67 while Matthew was away
summary: The laptop crashed at 08:01 while idle; nothing was lost, the five dashboard servers came back, and close_ticket.py was finally committed. While Matthew was away, Dress Up 0.0.62 to 0.0.67 shipped hugging legs, climbing a place's nearest ladder, the friend seen from behind, a one-off jump, and a game controller with a Controls tab (^ticket(136) to ^ticket(138)). The controller has only met a fake one (^ticket(139)).
next: ^ticket(133): try the drag fix on his device
every queued ticket waits on Matthew

title: Afternoon of 10-15: after the crash, Dress Up 0.0.42 to 0.0.45, two queue tags
summary: The laptop crashed at 15:33 during ^ticket(112); the game's edits survived, and an empty vibes.mp3 was made again and the music day republished. Dress Up 0.0.42 to 0.0.45 shipped a door behind the viewer, more side doors, readable signs, and a fix for drags that ground down while scenes animated (^ticket(117)): the scene had been rebuilt on every move. The queue gained long-run and blocked-on-Matthew tags.

title: Evening of 10-14: the autosave's print, B against C again, views in the worker
why: work done while Matthew was away
summary: The autosave's print was quadratic on the top-level let chain (^ticket(84)); fixed, a change's save went from about 600 ms to 80, profiled. #2597's heap grows per edit because its undo stack, capped only when a setting is on, keeps whole page models (^ticket(58)); Andrew's compaction from #2635 was ported. Views in the worker (^ticket(18)) cut main-thread work but slowed small slides; the other fixes were pushed 10-15 on Matthew's word.

title: Deep links (#2583): answers to the review
why: answering a PR review, at Matthew's ask
summary: Claude's answers, for Matthew to accept, change or drop, to the changes-requested review of #2583 (deep links). The review's main point holds: two URL encodings, parsing tangled with applying, and nothing testable without a browser. The plan: one request type parsed apart from applying, startup as an action in Main.re, and panel names in one switch in Sidebar.re; the branch is unchanged so far.
next: a request type with parse, to_params and tests
startup as an action; CopyDeepLink at the Page level
the panel-name switch, and the small fixes

title: ^ticket(45): what the page keeps, an audit
summary: On #2597, a Full Body tab's live heap grew about 85 MB per shirt-width slider edit, with no plateau. Experiments ruled out the whole-program memos, the undo history capped at 2, the projector view cache and ShareCodec's tables; heap snapshots crashed the tab, so V8's sampling profiler showed whole versions of the editor's state staying alive. An audit of every weak and strong table flagged four id-keyed tables.
next: count each flagged table's size per edit
give the growing table an owner and a lifetime

The dashboard now publishes by cron within a minute of a change.
